name: Arctiq Chiller 34 eSport Black
analog: Arctic Freezer 34 eSports, black (docs only, never shown in game)
desc: Single-tower 120 mm air cooler with four direct-touch heat pipes, all black.
doc_notes: Intel L17: fit the backplate under the board, screw the four standoffs through the board, lay the X bracket on top and tighten its four spring screws a few turns at a time in a cross pattern.
Arc V5: remove the board's plastic retention clips, keep the stock backplate, screw the four standoffs into it and fit the X bracket and its four spring screws in a cross pattern.
Peel the blue film off the base before mounting. Leaving it on will overheat the CPU.
Thermal paste: put a pea-sized dot (about 4 mm, 0.1 ml) in the middle of the CPU's heat spreader. The mounting pressure spreads it, so don't spread it yourself.
Plug the fan's 4-pin plug into the CPU_FAN header next to the socket; the board won't boot without a signal there.
Height 157 mm: check that your case has at least this much room for the CPU cooler.
Warranty: 3 years.

name: Tiron RM1 stock cooler
analog: Intel Laminar RM1 (docs only, never shown in game)
desc: The round boxed cooler from Tiron's L17 CPUs, paste already applied.
doc_notes: For Tiron L17 processors. The holes also fit the V5 boards in this game.
Pull the clear cap off the pre-applied paste. Don't touch the grey paste, and don't add more.
Lower the cooler straight down onto the CPU so the screws line up with the four holes round the socket.
Tighten the four spring screws a few turns at a time in a cross pattern until they stop.
Plug the fan's 4-pin plug into the CPU_FAN header next to the socket; the board won't boot without a signal there.
If you take the cooler off, clean both surfaces and use fresh paste: a pea-sized dot.
Rated for processors up to 65 W.
Warranty: 3 years with the boxed processor.

name: Arctiq Liquid Chiller II 240
analog: Arctic Liquid Freezer II 240 (docs only, never shown in game)
desc: 240 mm AIO with a thick 38 mm radiator and two 120 mm fans, black.
doc_notes: Fits Intel L17 and Arc V5. Use the matching standoffs and backplate (see the steps for your socket).
Peel the blue film off the cold plate before mounting, and the clear film off the pump cap.
Thermal paste: put a pea-sized dot (about 4 mm, 0.1 ml) in the middle of the CPU's heat spreader. The mounting pressure spreads it, so don't spread it yourself.
Mount the 240 mm radiator first, on the front or top fan positions. Keep the end tank with the tubes lower than the radiator's highest point, so any air collects away from the pump.
Never mount the radiator with the pump above it: the air would collect in the pump and make it rattle.
Front mount: the fans pull air in through the radiator from the front of the case. Top mount: they blow the air out through the top.
Plug the pump's 4-pin plug into the AIO_PUMP header, or into CPU_FAN set to full speed. Chain the radiator fans' plug into CPU_OPT or SYS_FAN.
Don't kink the tubes. Bend them no tighter than a 35 mm radius, and never cut or open them.
Warranty: 6 years.

name: Strata 1U heatsink SP-V
analog: Dynatron J2 1U SP5 heatsink (docs only, never shown in game)
desc: Passive 1U copper heatsink for Arc Epoch CPUs, cooled by the server's fan wall.
doc_notes: Fits socket SP-V only. Do not mount on desktop boards.
Peel the clear cover off the pre-applied thermal compound just before mounting. Do not touch the compound.
Line the fins up with the chassis airflow: the AIRFLOW arrow on the label points to the rear of the server.
Tighten the 6 captive T20 screws in the order printed on the label (1, 2, 3...) to 1.1-1.4 N m, then go round once more.
Loosen the screws in reverse order. Twist the heatsink gently to break the paste seal before lifting.
Passive heatsink: it needs the server's fan wall running and every blank fitted. Don't power on with the lid off for long.
Warranty: 3 years, return to the place of purchase with the proof of purchase.
